# AI/LLM Systems, VLA Model Serving (GGUF/ONNX/Pickle) & Commercial Datasets (`ai-llm-vla-model-serving-datasets`)

> **Group:** III. Enterprise, Data Lake & AI Systems
> **Product Archetypes:** AI_Model_Serving_Engine, Data_AI_Pipeline
> **Trigger Signals:** llm, vla, vlm, gguf, ggml, onnx, torch, pickle, safetensors, huggingface, prompt, mcp, dataset, asr, nlu, voice

## [ BLOCK: model-file-deserialization-and-binary-parsers ]
### Unsafe Model Loading (Pickle/Torch) & GGUF/ONNX Binary Parser Memory Safety
- Hunt for `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)`, `pickle.loads`, `joblib.load`, or `trust_remote_code=True` on external checkpoints.
- In C/C++ model loaders (`GGUF`, `ONNX`, tokenizer parsers like `vla.cpp`), check tensor dimension multiplication (`ne[0] * ne[1] * ...`), string length fields, and header offsets for integer overflow before memory allocation (`malloc`/`new`) leading to heap OOB read/write.

## [ BLOCK: ai-to-actuation-and-prompt-tool-boundaries ]
### Prompt/ASR-to-Physical Actuation & Tool/MCP Output Injection
- When ASR/NLU/LLM or VLA models connect to physical robot/vehicle controls or enterprise tools, verify whether a deterministic bounds/safety filter sits between model output and execution.
- Enforce instruction-data separation: treat all external documents, diagrams, and tool outputs as untrusted data, never executable instructions.

## [ BLOCK: model-upload-traversal-and-inference-resource-dos ]
### Model Artifact Path Traversal, ZipSlip & Inference Resource Exhaustion (API4)
- Audit model/adapter upload and HuggingFace/S3 download routines for path traversal (`../`), ZipSlip in `.pt`/`.zip` checkpoints, and SSRF via external model URLs.
- Check inference endpoints for missing token/tensor dimension caps, batch size limits, and request timeouts that allow GPU/memory OOM DoS.

### Standard Mappings
- NIST-AI-RMF, OWASP-LLM01, OWASP-LLM04, OWASP-LLM05, OWASP-API4:2023, ASVS-V5, CWE-190, CWE-502

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- SafeTensors or torch.load(..., weights_only=True) with SHA-256 signature verification on model checkpoints
- Checked 64-bit integer arithmetic (overflow guards on ne[0]*ne[1]*ne[2]*ne[3]) and bounds validation in C/C++ GGUF/ONNX parsers before allocation
- Deterministic kinematic/torque/velocity clamp and schema allowlist separating LLM/VLA/ASR outputs from physical actuators or tool execution

### Vulnerable Patterns
- torch.load(path) without weights_only=True, pickle.loads(), or AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True) on untrusted files
- Unchecked 32-bit/64-bit integer multiplication of tensor dimensions or header string lengths before malloc/new in C/C++ inference engines
- Forwarding LLM/ASR/NLU outputs directly to shell commands, SQL queries, MCP tools, or robot/vehicle control buses without deterministic safety validation

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of model loader / binary parser code showing deserialization and buffer allocation checks
- ev_... excerpt of inference endpoint and downstream tool/actuator dispatch logic

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Are model files loaded exclusively from a read-only, cryptographically signed internal artifact registry?
- Does a separate hardware safety controller clamp velocity/torque commands downstream of the VLA inference process?
